learningObjectives: Differentiate sympathetic, parasympathetic and enteric functions.
Identify major central autonomic network structures.
Explain how baroreflexes stabilise cardiovascular state.
Interpret autonomic symptoms without assuming a purely psychological cause.

anatomy.label: Insula
anatomy.detail: Posterior-to-anterior insular processing integrates interoceptive signals with salience and awareness.
anatomy.clinical: Altered interoceptive precision can amplify or blunt perceived bodily threat.

anatomy.label: Hypothalamus
anatomy.detail: Hypothalamic nuclei organise temperature, energy, fluid and defensive responses.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions or dysfunction can disturb appetite, sleep, thermoregulation and stress responses.

anatomy.label: Brainstem autonomic nuclei
anatomy.detail: NTS and medullary networks integrate visceral afferents and regulate output.
anatomy.clinical: Dysfunction can impair blood-pressure, respiratory or swallowing control.

anatomy.label: Sympathetic pathways
anatomy.detail: Thoracolumbar preganglionic neurons recruit distributed organs through ganglia.
anatomy.clinical: Excess or inadequate responses can produce tachycardia, sweating or orthostatic symptoms.

anatomy.label: Parasympathetic pathways
anatomy.detail: Craniosacral output, especially vagal pathways, regulates heart, lungs and gut.
anatomy.clinical: Vagal effects are organ-specific; “more vagal” is not universally better.

interaction.title: Explore the Autonomic Nervous System
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Sense
stages.text: Visceral receptors report pressure, chemistry and organ state.

stages.label: Integrate
stages.text: Brainstem, hypothalamic and cortical regions interpret current demand.

stages.label: Mobilise
stages.text: Sympathetic output reallocates energy and supports action when needed.

stages.label: Restore
stages.text: Parasympathetic pathways support recovery, digestion and conservation.

stages.label: Update
stages.text: Interoception and learning influence how future bodily changes are interpreted.

quizBank.question: Preganglionic sympathetic neurons arise primarily from the:
quizBank.explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons originate in thoracic and upper lumbar spinal segments.

quizBank.question: The nucleus tractus solitarius primarily receives:
quizBank.explanation: The NTS is a major brainstem relay for cardiovascular, respiratory and gastrointestinal afferents.

quizBank.question: Which structure is central to conscious interoceptive representation?
quizBank.explanation: The insula integrates internal bodily signals with salience and subjective awareness.

quizBank.question: The baroreflex helps stabilise:
quizBank.explanation: Stretch receptors and brainstem circuits rapidly adjust heart and vascular output.

quizBank.question: Which statement is most accurate?
options: Autonomic patterns are context-dependent and not diagnosis-specific
quizBank.explanation: Autonomic states are real but psychologically non-specific; interpretation requires context and differential assessment.

prompts: Name the major components of the Autonomic Nervous System.
